Click HERE to watch his full pre-match media conference. The men in purple will head into the Round 4 fixture at HBF Park bolstered by last weekend’s emphatic and eye-catching 4-0 home victory over Adelaide United in which Jaiden Kucharski, Tadi Kuzamba, Stefan Colakovski and Matt Ellis all found the net. But Griffiths insisted that he believes his side have plenty more to give. “It’s been a really positive week of training again which is what we wanted,” he said “We wanted to stay grounded and focused on the next game against the Premiers. “The boys have been training really well and we’re expecting another big performance. “We just need to stick to our process and look at what we can improve and making sure the players know where we need to improve. “We did that last week and we did exactly the same this week; focusing on how do we get better as a team because we’re still a mile off where we need to be and as we play more games, we’ll learn more about ourselves and continue to improve.” The Head Coach went on to claim that the Jets, who are yet to win a game in either the A-League or the AFC Champions League so far this term, are a much better side than their recent form suggests. “They are a quality team who have been a bit unlucky in their early games in the A-League,” he said. “They’ve got [Nikos] Vergos, they’ve got [Joe] Lolley, they’ve got a lot quality in that front third, so we’ve got to make sure that we restrict them, but at the same time, stick to our playing our own game.” Glory will be forced to take on the Jets without Tom Lawrence as her serves a one-match suspension, but Griffiths feels that the squad can adapt successfully to the skipper’s enforced absence. “Tom is a big part of what we do,” he said, “but at the same time, we’ve been building a squad so that we’re not reliant on one particular player. “In saying that, he’s a quality player that we do have to replace, but I feel that the leadership within the group and the expectation of the group and of individuals needs to step up and make space for someone else to shine and that excites me.” In other early team news, Trent Ostler is set to come into the selection frame this weekend after recovering from injury and although none of the club’s other sidelined players will be available, Griffiths confirmed that he is hopeful Charbel Shamoon could be back shortly. He concluded by acknowledging the role the club’s Members and fans will have to play once again at HBF Park. “They make a massive difference,” he said. “We play for them and we want that excitement and we want that energy at HBF. “They are everything about the club and we appreciate their support.” The Jets will make the long trip west still searching for a first win of the season having drawn with the Mariners and Macarthur FC in the opening two rounds before being downed 3-0 at home by Wellington last time out. Mark Milligan’s side have also found life tough in the AFC Champions League, suffering four defeats so far against admittedly very high-quality opposition in the form of Gamba Osaka, Shanghai Port, Kyoto Sanga and Kashima Antlers. In addition to ex-Sydney FC dangerman Lolley, who is poised to make his 100th ALM appearance and combative Greek striker Vergos, other payers to look out for in the opposition’s ranks include English midfield creator Zach Clough and former Glory defender Alex Grant. Saturday will mark the 61st meeting between the two sides, with Glory having enjoyed 29 wins to the Jets’ 13. 16 of those victories for the WA side have come at home where they have outscored the Jets by 56 goals to 36. MATCH REPORT: Newcastle Jets vs Shanghai Port Newcastle Jets Media 3 November, 2026 Share Share Share this link via Share this: Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Share on X (Opens in new window) X Or Copy Link Copy Match Reports Shanghai Port defeated the Newcastle Jets 4-2 in the AFC Champions League Elite Shanghai dominated possession and chances in the opening minutes of the match, with Delianov being forced into making several saves. Leonardo opened the scoring for Shanghai in the 23rd minute, nodding the ball into the back of the net from close range. Things would be compounded in the 26th minute, with Aquilina turning the ball into his own net following a dangerous ball from Melendo. The Jets started to show some positive signs towards the end of the half, having several near misses including Patrick Wood skewing a shot wide. Joel Bertolissio also fired one low across the 6-yard box right before half-time, but wasn’t able to find the feet of any of his teammates. Shanghai took their two goal advantage into the break. Prince Ampen added a third for the visitors shortly after halftime, smashing the ball into the bottom corner at the far post. Patrick Wood would give us a lifeline in the 58th minute, taking Badolato’s cross in his stride before tucking the ball past Yan Junling in the Shanghai goal. Patrick Wood’s goal against Shanghai pushed him to the top of our all time AFC goalscorers Xavier Bertoncello added a second in the 80th minute. A nice passage of play saw the Jets work the ball from the right flank to the left, where Xavier curled the ball around the keeper and into the net. The late comeback would be shot down by Shanghai, as Xinxiang Li added a fourth, stretching to poke the ball past Delianov. Full-time would soon follow, with the visitors running out as 4-2 winners. Share facebook x email Leeds United will be keen to get back to winning ways on Saturday lunchtime as they welcome Tottenham Hotspur to Elland Road. The Whites fell to defeat for just the second time this campaign last time out at AFC Bournemouth. Daniel Farke’s side dominated the opening stages and thought they had taken the lead through Dominic Calvert-Lewin, until VAR chalked the goal off after the ball had struck the England international’s hand. A mistake at the back then saw the Cherries take the lead and as United threw everything forward in search of an equaliser, the hosts added a second on the break. Prior to that one on the south coast, Leeds had earned a valuable point on Wearside with a goalless draw against Sunderland. In an encounter hampered by the conditions, neither team were able to break the deadlock as the defences came out on top. Leeds sit 12th in the standings after those results, one point adrift of a resurgent Spurs side. After surviving on the final day of the season last campaign, there was a big overhaul to the squad in the summer and, understandably, the new faces needed time to settle in under Roberto De Zerbi. Having struggled for form in their opening few games, the London outfit have since picked up three victories in a row heading into Saturday’s encounter. That run started with a 3-1 win over Coventry City on home soil, before a rare success at Stamford Bridge saw Spurs beat rivals Chelsea 2-0. Last time out, goals from former United youngster Archie Gray and defender Jan Paul van Hecke proved enough against Crystal Palace. The most recent meeting between the two sides came towards the end of the previous term. Mathys Tel opened the scoring for the hosts at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium but after the forward had given away a penalty in the second half, up stepped Calvert-Lewin to earn the Whites a deserved point. Action from Elland Road gets underway at 12.30pm. The view from inside the camp: Speaking exclusively to Premeir League Studios, Jayden Bogle said: "I think you have to be respectful of the fact that they're a big club with fantastic players. But again, it's so early in the league. Everyone's close together. You can't really pay too much attention to league position at the moment. We're full of confidence. I'm sure they'll be full of confidence. I think it'll be a good game." Read the full interview here . Team News: In his pre-match press conference, the boss said Joe Rodon is in contention to feature after returning to team training. Dominic Calvert-Lewin is a slight doubt but expected to be fit while question marks remain on the fitness of Anton Stach and Noah Okafor. Remembrance: Leeds United will pay its respects to those who have served our country on Saturday afternoon as we take on Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League, with a special tribute and moment of silence held prior to kick-off. Our dedicated Remembrance fixture, which is always the closest home game to Remembrance Day, will feature a number of activities as we commemorate the sacrifices of servicemen and women and their families, past and present. Find out more here . Supporter information: Discriminatory language or chanting, including tragedy chanting, is not acceptable, and you could be breaking the law. The club condemns this behaviour and has a zero-tolerance policy towards discrimination abuse of all kinds. To report an incident, text LEEDS along with any relevant information including ticket details, your name and description of an incident to 60006. You will then receive an automated response which means that your report has been logged and will then be looked into. Tough measures and sanctions are in place across all English football leagues to tackle dangerous and illegal behaviours within football grounds, and this involves but is not limited to, discriminatory behaviour, tragedy chanting, fans entering the pitch, the use of pyros and throwing objects. A list of prohibited items can be found HERE . Parking update: All parking (including accessible and motorcycle spaces) for the Elland Road Council Car Parks has SOLD OUT . Please do not travel in your vehicle to Elland Road without a pre-booked parking ticket. Supporters arriving without a pre-booked space will be turned away. Off-site car parking remains available at the White Rose Office Park . Spaces must be pre-booked for matchday. More information can be found here . Stadium redevelopment updates: Due to the redevelopment of the West Stand at Elland Road, there will be a significant change to the way West Stand ticket holders will access the stadium on matchdays throughout the 2026/27 season. The main West Stand Gate on Elland Road (next to Howard’s) will now be the main access point for away fans only. This will also be the only access point for home supporters with tickets in areas C15, C16 & C17 when an away team fails to sell their full allocation and supporters with designated accessible tickets in the South Stand Lower area FA6. No other supporters will be able to access the West Stand via this route. All general admission West Stand ticket holders (with the exception of the above) will enter through Entrances 4, 5, and 6. You can access these areas via Gate 4 from Lowfields Road (North East Corner), Gate 2 on Bobby Collins Way (behind the North Stand), or Gate 1 from Bobby Collins Way (North West Corner). Find out more here . How to follow: Fans around the world can listen to every minute of Saturday’s fixture LIVE on LUTV. Bryn Law will be joined by Tony Dorigo on commentary. Pre-match build up begins at 12pm with Jermaine Beckford and Stuart Dallas in the studio! The match has also been selected for live TV coverage on Sky Sports for viewers in the UK. What has the boss said: The latest FPL advice from Fantasy Football Scout: Ethan Ampadu’s (£5.3m) consistency in FPL last season made him an excellent differential pick. He started 35 games, which was the most of any Leeds player. The skipper also racked up a total of 134 points, which was bettered only by Dominic Calvert-Lewin (£6.1m) and Anton Stach (£6.0m) within the Whites’ squad. Making up his haul, the Welshman scored one goal, assisted four, earned eight clean sheets and received 11 bonus points. He completed the most defensive actions (416) across the entirety of the Leeds squad, hitting the threshold for Defensive Contribution points in 54.3 per cent of matches. Read more here . 'Fine margins' - Jayden Bogle reveals Thorp Arch focus ahead of Spurs visit - Leeds United leedsunited.com leedsunited.com Tickets LUTV SHOP News Tickets & Hospitality Men Women Academy Memberships Events More... search trigger burger menu Previous Next Mens 'Fine margins' - Jayden Bogle reveals Thorp Arch focus ahead of Spurs visit 05 Nov 26 Defender addresses mood in the camp before Elland Road early kick-off. Share facebook x email Jayden Bogle says Leeds United are working on fine details to remedy their main issue but remain in a good place ahead of the visit of Tottenham Hotspur. The Whites host Spurs in Saturday's early kick-off and Bogle insists the mood in the camp is as strong as it was prior to last weekend's defeat at Bournemouth. "I still think we're in a good place now," he exclusively told Premier League Studios. "But it's just, like people said after the game, the fine margins with the decision-making, probably in the final third, just to turn those draws into wins and take those chances when we can. "But I think the morale of the group and the confidence and everything is still there. We're still 100 per cent behind each other and the staff and we'll still want to give everything for the club. And I just think it's those tiny details, and especially in the final third. If we can click, we'll start turning the majority of those draws into wins." Spurs sit three places and one point ahead of Leeds in the Premier League table going into the game, with a goal difference of zero compared to the Whites' plus one. "I think you have to be respectful of the fact that they're a big club with fantastic players," said Bogle. "But again, it's so early in the league. Everyone's close together. You can't really pay too much attention to league position at the moment. We're full of confidence. I'm sure they'll be full of confidence. I think it'll be a good game." The preparations at Thorp Arch this week have been as expected, with a focus on final third efficiency. "Just normal," said Bogle. "Nothing changed. Like I said, we're working on those fine details to just almost click in the final third and get those goals flowing again because we haven't scored as much as we'd probably want to at the moment. We're working on that to be the best in that aspect and hopefully the rest takes care of itself." Cántabros y andaluces, que se han visto las caras en Segunda División los dos últimos cursos y ascendieron juntos a la elite (los primeros como campeones y los segundos vía play off), se reencuentran en LaLiga EA Sports después de 15 temporadas. Los verdiblancos buscarán sumar sus primeros puntos a domicilio de la temporada 2026/27 y para ello contarán como aval con los empates conseguidos en sus dos últimas visitas al feudo blanquiazul (1-1 y 0-0). Los precedentes más recientes en la elite, sin embargo, se decantaron del lado malagueño y la victoria verdiblanca más reciente en la máxima categoría data del 19 de septiembre de 2009 . Es hora de dejarla atrás y convertirla en la anteúltima. Recuerdo a Jesús de Miguel  Mantilla y Andrés , por lesión, son las dos bajas racinguistas para este partido, para el que José Alberto  ha convocado al lateral del Rayo Cantabria Hugo Pérez y en el que se recordará al delantero del Club Deportivo Tenerife   Jesús de Miguel fallecido esta semana. Ambos conjuntos saldrán con una camiseta conmemorativa y en el minuto nueve -dorsal que llevaba el jugador- se detendrá el encuentro y se guardará silencio en su memoria. Éxito de Funes Juan Funes , uno de los principales artífices del retorno del Málaga CF a Primera (promocionó al primer equipo desde el filial), tiene a su equipo colista con cinco puntos y el casillero de triunfos como local sin inaugurar. Por este motivo, aunque apenas se haya disputado el primer tercio de la presente edición de LaLiga EA Sports, los puntos en juego valen su peso en oro.    Los andaluces, que han sumado cinco empates ante el Deportivo Alavés, el Real Club Deportivo Espanyol, el Celta, el Levante UD y el Deportivo (tres en La Rosaleda y dos a domicilio) tienen en Adrián Niño , con cinco tantos hasta la fecha, como principal baza ofensiva; Chupe suma dos en Copa al que firmó en LaLiga y Dani Lorenzo, Dotor y Pablo Martínez, con uno, son las amenazas desde la segunda línea. El encuentro entre cántabros y blanquiazules supondrá el regreso a Málaga de José Alberto y Pablo Álvarez , que ocuparon el banquillo local de La Rosaleda la temporada 2021/22 en Segunda División. Un año después ambos técnicos se incorporaron al Racing, cuya clasificación fueron mejorando en la categoría de plata campaña tras campaña hasta conseguir, el pasado mayo, el ascenso a Primera y el título de campeón de LaLiga Hypermotion. La sesión no contó con la presencia de los lesionados Mantilla y Andrés , pero sí con Hugo Pérez , del Rayo Cantabria, que entra en la convocatoria. José Alberto comenzó la rueda de prensa reconociendo que “ l a semana ha sido dura porque el fútbol queda en un segundo plano ” y aprovechó para “enviar mi más sentido pésame y un fuerte abrazo a la familia de Jesús y la plantilla del Club Deportivo Tenerife”. El técnico verdiblanco aseguró que “ queremos trasladar nuestra personalidad como locales a los partidos de fuera de casa , no tener lagunas y sí mucha contundencia para traernos los tres puntos”. Además, señaló que los análisis de los rivales se basan en “sus virtudes y defectos, y las características de sus jugadores” y que el Málaga “ está dando continuidad a la plantilla y el buen hacer de la temporada pasada , pero ha tenido un calendario complicado”. Mantilla El nombre propio de la rueda de prensa fue Mantilla : “ Está bien , fastidiado por perderse la temporada, pero es un gladiador, es muy fuerte y ya está descontando días para volver ”. Y en la misma línea de las bajas, afirmó que “ tenemos una plantilla con soluciones y herramientas para afrontar cualquier baja . Los jugadores están preparados para suplirlas con las mayores garantías posibles, que es para lo que trabajan”. Y concluyó subrayando que “ todos los jugadores tienen la puerta abierta a tener más minutos , aunque depende de la posición”, concretando en la figura de Íñigo , que “siempre está deseando tener minutos y yo, como entrenador, también estoy deseando dárselos porque se lo merece”. Spazio anche ai giovani, da Sugamele a Trepy, e alle condizioni del gruppo: «Giochiamo in casa, dopo quattro sconfitte vogliamo tornare a fare tre punti». GLI INDISPONIBILI «Non ci saranno Fadera, che ha riportato una lesione al bicipite femorale, Nzola, che ha accusato una lesione muscolare dopo la partita, e Mina, anche lui alle prese con una lesione al bicipite femorale. Aurelio ha una lesione di basso grado al soleo. Obert, oltre a essere squalificato, ha una sofferenza al ginocchio. Restano a casa anche Idrissi e Felici. Porteremo con noi Prettenhoffer dall’Under 20». L’AVVERSARIO «Quando analizziamo gli avversari ne studiamo i punti di forza e quelli deboli. Il Frosinone ha qualità individuali importanti, a partire da Ghedjemis ma non solo. Stimo molto anche Kvernadze: sono anni che lo seguo e sono sempre stato convinto del suo valore. Mi dispiace che domani non ci sia Raimondo. L’anno scorso diversi di questi ragazzi giocavano in Serie B e oggi stanno facendo la differenza. Questo dimostra che in quella categoria ci sono tanti calciatori validi, che hanno bisogno di fiducia e coraggio per emergere». L’IDENTITÀ DEL FROSINONE E ALVINI «Il Frosinone ha un’identità chiara e precisa. Lo abbiamo affrontato lo scorso anno in Coppa Italia e conosciamo il valore di alcuni suoi giocatori, come Schmid, capaci di spostare gli equilibri. Anche gli esterni sono importanti e dovremo essere bravi a portarli fuori dalla loro zona di comfort, perché è una squadra che concede qualcosa. Alvini è un allenatore forte e importante, lo era già quando allenava la Cremonese, anche se in quel caso non ha avuto la stessa fortuna. Ha un gruppo di ragazzi che lo segue e una visione di gioco ben definita, indipendentemente dall’assetto tattico. Le sue squadre hanno idee precise e un’identità forte: vanno uomo contro uomo su tutto il campo. Il Frosinone mi piace. È una squadra che ha fame e una chimica interna che le permette di andare oltre le aspettative. Mi piace anche il modo in cui festeggia sotto la Curva: si percepisce il legame che si è creato con il proprio pubblico». L’IMPORTANZA DELLA PARTITA «È una partita particolare, ma il Frosinone va trattato come tutte le altre avversarie: non sottovalutiamo nessuno. Qualcuno pensava che fosse nelle prime posizioni per caso, ma non è una valutazione che condivido. Non so fin dove potrà arrivare, ma ha dimostrato di avere valori importanti. Serviranno energia e caratteristiche adatte alla partita. Noi vogliamo vincere e dovremo essere bravi a imporre il nostro gioco, limitando le qualità del Frosinone. Giochiamo in casa e, dopo quattro sconfitte, vogliamo tornare a conquistare i tre punti. Dovremo farlo senza frenesia, mantenendo lucidità e pazienza». IL PUBBLICO ROSSOBLÙ «Siamo dispiaciuti quanto i nostri tifosi. Non vincere da quattro partite lascia inevitabilmente amarezza, ma vogliamo ringraziarli per il sostegno continuo che ci stanno dimostrando. A Roma credo abbiano apprezzato il fatto che la squadra abbia dato tutto. È quello che dobbiamo fare sempre. Il pubblico può fare la differenza e noi abbiamo bisogno del suo supporto». LA FIDUCIA NEI GIOVANI E SUGAMELE «In questi quattordici mesi si è visto che guardo tutti e tutto: non ho problemi a far giocare Sugamele. Lo conosciamo bene, ha qualità importanti e va gestito con attenzione, come Kofler. Ha un potenziale notevole, personalità ed è un ragazzo cinico. Rappresenta il futuro del calcio italiano e gli auguro che questo sia soltanto l’inizio di un percorso importante. Abbiamo cercato di costruire un rapporto sempre più stretto tra Under 20 e Prima squadra, anche creando uno spazio condiviso per favorire la conoscenza e il senso di gruppo. Sugamele domani potrebbe anche giocare. Il Cagliari deve saper mettere al centro l’interesse comune, non quello personale». LE POSSIBILI SOLUZIONI TATTICHE «Quando parlo della possibilità di cambiare modulo, penso anche a soluzioni come Sugawara o Trepy. Ho diverse opzioni a disposizione e valuterò fino all’ultimo: non prenderò una decisione definitiva prima di domani mattina». TREPY «Trepy può partire dal primo minuto. A Roma ci ha permesso di avere maggiore profondità e sta crescendo. So quello che può darci e sono contento del suo percorso: è un ragazzo che può rappresentare una soluzione importante per noi». LE CONDIZIONI DEI SINGOLI: RODRIGUEZ «Rodriguez è un ragazzo con una personalità forte, ma deve migliorare ancora tanto. Dopo gli impegni con la Nazionale ha perso qualcosa, così come è successo a Romano, Maldini e Obert, che hanno vissuto una sosta lunga e ne hanno risentito. Rodriguez ha caratteristiche interessanti e, se saprà mantenere la fame giusta, potrà diventare un giocatore importante. Ha ancora diversi aspetti da sviluppare, anche perché arriva da un calcio diverso». MENDY E IL PERCORSO DI CRESCITA «Paul è un ragazzo con la testa sulle spalle. Nelle ultime due partite è partito dalla panchina per una scelta legata alla gestione della condizione fisica: aveva bisogno di rifiatare. Quando è entrato, però, lo ha fatto con il piglio giusto. Per lui è il coronamento di un sogno, ma adesso deve essere bravo a gestire questo momento, senza mai rilassarsi. Ha ancora tanta strada da fare». LE CONDIZIONI DI WINKS «Winks sta bene ed è recuperato. Avrebbe potuto giocare anche contro la Lazio, ma abbiamo preferito non rischiarlo. Ora è a disposizione». LE SCELTE SULLA FASCIA SINISTRA «A sinistra abbiamo ancora un dubbio. Rodriguez può ricoprire quel ruolo, come ha già fatto lo scorso anno contro il Napoli, ma dobbiamo riflettere bene per capire se sia la scelta più adatta oppure se sia preferibile modificare l’assetto. Valuteremo tutte le possibilità». LA GESTIONE DEGLI EPISODI «Dobbiamo essere più lucidi e non portarci dietro gli episodi che ci hanno penalizzato nelle ultime partite. Continuare a pensarci significa non riuscire a recuperare le energie, soprattutto dal punto di vista mentale. Bisogna voltare pagina e concentrarsi su quello che possiamo fare in campo». We’ve been talking lately about how a win should be the natural result of doing many things well. We’re very excited and highly motivated; the victory the other day gave us an extra boost of energy,” said Sarabia. “I’ve encountered a squad here with a tremendous willingness to work. We want to connect with the fans, for them to help us, push us on, and feel proud of the team. It will be a tough game, and we’ll need to do a lot of things right to get a win.” The coach also noted that “We haven’t had much time to work on everything, but as I said, we have to be intelligent and create the right conditions for our players to feel comfortable, so we can keep building. We’re ready to win, though it will take more time to fully refine the style of play we’re aiming for.” Regarding Deportivo, a newly promoted side from the Segunda División who have been performing well in their return to the top flight, he remarked that “They’re a side with plenty of resources -in particular their fast players who combine well. It’s going to be a great battle between two teams that both favour a proactive, dominant approach and want to spend as much time as possible in the opposition half.” Sarabia emphasised that, this Saturday, “the focus is on being competitive, hungry, and brave, and on connecting with the fans. That’s what we want to see, because, over time, it will make us stronger. We will build upon many aspects from the Villarreal win to keep growing.” With a laugh, he concluded by saying “I’ve told the players that by the next international break, I want two more of them to be called up for their national teams” -referring to Roberto, Javi Hernández, and Vanja, who have received call-ups this time around. El Dépor visita al RCD Espanyol "con la preparación a ciegas" por la llegada de Eder Sarabia al banquillo espanyolista pero "preparados para cualquier situación" | Real Club Deportivo de A Coruña Actualidad Actualidad Equipos Equipos Club Club Academy Academy Fundación Fundación Deportivismo Deportivismo Experiencias Experiencias Tienda oficial Tienda oficial Museo&Tour Museo&Tour Hospitality Hospitality Entradas Entradas Cuenta Cuenta Volver DÉPOR · 6 NOVIEMBRE 2026 EL DÉPOR VISITA AL RCD ESPANYOL "CON LA PREPARACIÓN A CIEGAS" POR LA LLEGADA DE EDER SARABIA AL BANQUILLO ESPANYOLISTA PERO "PREPARADOS PARA CUALQUIER SITUACIÓN" El Dépor visita al RCD Espanyol este sábado 7 de noviembre a las 16:15 (Dazn) en el RCDE Stadium, en partido correspondiente a la 12ª jornada en LaLiga EA Sports. Antonio Hidalgo admite que la preparación del partido es "a ciegas porque no sabes exactamente lo que te puedes encontrar" por la llegada esta misma semana de Eder Sarabia al banquillo espanyolista. "Todos lo conocemos y como quiere que sus equipos puedan jugar, qué ideas puedan tener. Uno se puede hacer una idea en la cabeza de lo que se puede encontrar mañana pero hasta que ruede el balón no sabemos exactamente lo que va a pasar", añadió. Eso sí, el técnico deportivista afirma que "tenemos que estar preparados para cualquier situación, poder contemplar diferentes opciones". Tras el triunfo del pasado lunes ante CA Osasuna en ABANCA-RIAZOR, Os Nosos llegan al choque con 14 puntos en la 8ª posición. El Dépor completó este mismo viernes una última sesión de entrenamiento en el Dépor Training Center con una activación, un ensayo de acciones a balón parado, un ejercicio táctico y fútbol reducido para concluir. Kevin Sánchez y Noé fueron los representantes de ANOSACANTEIRA. En el grupo estuvo Marc Casadó, del que Antonio Hidalgo manifestó que "está con muchísimas ganas. Tenemos que ir viendo los momentos en los que pueda estar. Está completando los entrenamientos con absoluta normalidad. Tenemos que tener ese punto de cautela, sabiendo que hay un parón por medio para darle también su tiempo". Insiste en que "se encuentra bien, con ganas. Su cabeza le empuja mucho hacia adelante. Los doctores dicen que está soldado. Yo lo veo contento y eso es importante". Alternan tareas con el grupo y con el readaptador Zakaria Eddahchouri y Brihgt Ede. Del delantero holandés el entrenador del Dépor afirma que su regreso "cada vez está más cerca. Tiene muchísimas ganas. No sé decirte exactamente cuando pero tiene pinta que va a ser pronto. Encantado de tenerle de vuelta en cuanto eso pase". Y del central polaco Antonio Hidalgo explicó que "está completando partes del entrenamiento. Arriesgar sabiendo que hay un parón por delante y que después va a estar en perfectas condiciones no tenía sentido. Creemos que para la vuelta del parón va a estar perfecto". Por su parte, el RCD Espanyol, que venció en La Cerámica al Villarreal CF (0-1), es 14º con 11 puntos. En su campo esta temporada los catalanes vencieron al Levante UD (3-0); empataron con el Sevilla FC (1-1); y cayeron con el Real Madrid CF (1-2), Elche CF (1-3) y Atlético de Madrid (0-1). Los espanyolistas se llevaron una alegría por la convocatoria de Roberto Fernández con la selección española, de Javi Hernández con la sub-21 y de Vanja Drkušić, con Eslovenia. En su presentación como entrenador, este pasado miércoles 4 de noviembre, Eder Sarabia confiesa que le gusta "ser rebelde, ser valiente, ir un poco contra algunas cosas establecidas pero sobre todo esa rebeldía para sacar lo mejor de cada uno y para que el futbolista, cada vez que entre a un terreno de juego sienta que tiene el poder de que pasen las cosas que él quiere que pasen". Se propone "recuperar el RCDE del 125 aniversario. Con esa energía, esa ilusión y esa conexión con la afición. Queremos volver a vivir días mágicos en el Estadio". Finalizado el encuentro, Os Nosos se entrenarán de nuevo el martes 10 de noviembre a las 17:00 en el Dépor Training Center. Match Preview presented by DigAlert: LA Galaxy at Real Salt Lake | November 7, 2026 | LA Galaxy Skip to main content Tickets Schedule Roster Club News Academy Stadium Community Video Youth Cozmo Ventura County FC Español Store STM HQ English Español English Tickets Schedule Roster Club News Academy Stadium Community Video Youth Cozmo Ventura County FC Español English Español English Store STM HQ Tickets Schedule Roster Club News Academy Stadium Community Video Youth Cozmo Ventura County FC Español STM HQ English Español English Store Match Preview Match Preview presented by DigAlert: LA Galaxy at Real Salt Lake | November 7, 2026 LA Galaxy Communications Copy URL Share on Facebook Share on X LOS ANGELES (November 6, 2026) – The LA Galaxy are set to conclude the MLS regular season on Saturday, November 7 against Real Salt Lake at America First Field in Sandy, Utah (4 p.m. PT, Apple TV). With one match remaining, the Galaxy occupy seventh place in the Western Conference standings on 44 points, holding a two-point advantage over 11th-place Real Salt Lake as both clubs pursue postseason positioning. Playoff Clinching Scenarios The Galaxy can finish no higher than seventh place in the Western Conference and control their own playoff destiny entering Decision Day. A win at Real Salt Lake would secure a postseason berth and a matchup with the conference's second-place finisher, currently FC Dallas, in the Round One Best-of-3 Series. A draw could also be enough for LA to advance if at least one of Portland, Colorado or Seattle drops points on the final day. If the Galaxy fall to Real Salt Lake, they would need help elsewhere around the Western Conference to reach the playoffs. Should teams finish level on points, total wins serve as the first tiebreaker, followed by goal differential. Read more about the Galaxy's clinching scenarios HERE . LA Galaxy vs Real Salt Lake The Galaxy enter Saturday's match having won three of their last five meetings against Real Salt Lake, including a 2-1 victory earlier this season. In that April matchup, Marco Reus scored both goals for LA, converting an 85th-minute penalty to secure all three points. The clubs split their two meetings in 2025, with the Galaxy responding to a road defeat with a 2-0 win at Dignity Health Sports Park behind goals from Lucas Sanabria and Joseph Paintsil. Saturday's contest features a pair of notable connections between the two sides. Pablo Ruiz is set to face Real Salt Lake for the first time since joining the Galaxy during the 2026 summer transfer window, while brothers Lucas Sanabria and Juan Manuel Sanabria will line up on opposite sides. Overall, LA holds a 23-18-13 advantage in the all-time regular-season series between the clubs. Recent Results Over the last five matches, the Galaxy have posted a 2-1-2 record, earning points in four of their five October contests. During that stretch, LA registered wins over the Portland Timbers and Austin FC, draws against San Diego FC and LAFC, and a road loss to St. Louis CITY SC. Most recently, the Galaxy delivered one of their strongest performances of the season with a 4-1 victory over Austin. The result continued a strong run of form for LA, which has compiled 18 points on a 5-2-3 record across its last 10 matches. During that span, the Galaxy overcame deficits to defeat Colorado Rapids and Minnesota United FC, recorded a clean-sheet victory against the Portland Timbers, and tied a season high with four goals scored in a 4-1 win over Austin FC. Standout Performances The Galaxy's recent run of form has coincided with attacking contributions from throughout the roster. João Klauss has tallied five goals and an assist over his last seven matches, reaching double-digit league goals with his strike against Austin FC. Marco Reus continues to lead LA's attack with 12 goal contributions in his last nine appearances, highlighted by a season-high three assists against Austin and his sixth MLS Team of the Matchday selection of the season. Meanwhile, Robert Taylor has contributed six goal contributions (two goals, four assists) across the club's last seven matches. Hirving Lozano marked his return from an injury suffered on international duty with the game-winning goal against Austin, while Sergi Roberto recorded his first goal for the Galaxy and added an assist as his midfield partnership with Pablo Ruiz continues to develop. Homegrown defender Harbor Miller registered the first multi-contribution performance of his MLS career with two assists against Austin, earning a place on the MLS Team of the Matchday bench. "Immer voll da sein" Donnerstag | 05.11.2026 | 14:48 Uhr SCP07 empfängt am Samstag Eintracht Frankfurt Unser Sportclub spielt am Samstag (15.30 Uhr) in der Bundesliga zu Hause in der ausverkauften Home Deluxe Arena gegen Eintracht Frankfurt. Bei der Pressekonferenz vor der Partie saß neben Cheftrainer Ralf Kettemann auch Außenbahnspieler Laurin Curda auf dem Podium.  Vorschau Vor der Länderspielpause geht es für unseren SCP07 noch mal um wichtige Punkte gegen Frankfurt. Für Curda ist klar: "In der Bundesliga muss man immer voll da sein. Es hat etwas gedauert, bis wir reingekommen sind, aber wir haben uns gut angepasst und mittlerweile sieht man, was wir draufhaben.“ Personal Fehlen werden Timur Gayret, Nyamekye Awortwie-Grant und Marcel Hoffmeier. Ansonsten sind alle Spieler einsatzbereit – natürlich auch Curda, der sich nach der Roten Karte im DFB-Pokal gegen den VfB Stuttgart schnell wieder auf die Bundesliga konzentriert hat. "Am Tag des Pokalspiels ging es mir bescheiden. Vor allem, wenn man sieht, was möglich gewesen wäre. Ich habe aber daraus gelernt und bin reifer geworden", sagte er. Für den kommenden Gegner hatte er lobende Worte parat: "Frankfurt hat gute Einzelspieler und ist sehr stark im Umschaltspiel. Da müssen wir aufpassen. Aber wir haben gezeigt, was wir draufhaben. Wir müssen unser Spiel einfach durchziehen, dann wird es eine spannende Partie.“ Gegner Die Frankfurter haben sich zuletzt durch zwei 3:1-Siege gegen den Hamburger SV (DFB-Pokal und Bundesliga) etwas Luft verschafft. In der Tabelle stehen aktuell elf Punkte und Rang acht zu Buche. Ziel ist es, weiter Stabilität in die Leistungen und Ergebnisse zu bekommen. Richtig gut drauf ist Stürmer Younes Ebnoutalib, der sechs Treffer in acht Spielen erzielt hat und in der kommenden Woche auch wieder bei der deutschen Nationalmannschaft dabei sein wird. Jonathan Burkardt, der auch bereits in der Nationalmannschaft gespielt hat, traf bisher dreimal. "Frankfurt ist eine super Bundesliga-Mannschaft, die mittlerweile die Kurve bekommen hat. Wir müssen den Fokus darauf legen, gemeinsam diese Offensivkraft zu verteidigen", betonte Kettemann. Mit von der Partie sein wird auch Mario Götze, der in der Home Deluxe Arena auf seinen Bruder und Sportclub-Kapitän Felix treffen wird. "Jano ter Horst ist ein sehr physischer Spieler, während Felix am Ball ruhiger agiert. Beide haben ihre Vorteile. Wir müssen schauen, was es braucht, um dieses Spiel zu gewinnen", sagte der Cheftrainer.  Infos Die Home Deluxe Arena ist ausverkauft, 15.000 Zuschauer werden dabei sein, davon 1500 Gästefans. Eine Tageskasse wird deshalb nicht angeboten.  Schiedsrichter der Partie ist Bastian Dankert.  ACHTUNG: Seit dieser Saison steht den Fans auf dem Vorplatz der Home Deluxe Arena ein neuer Biergarten zur Verfügung. Beim Heimspiel gegen Frankfurt öffnet dieser um 13 Uhr.  Der Fanshop auf dem Stadion-Vorplatz hat ab 10 Uhr geöffnet, bis 30 Minuten nach Spielende.  Der Heim-Bereich ist 90 Minuten vor Anpfiff, der Hospitality-Bereich ist bereits 120 Minuten vor Anpfiff offen. fixture before the season’s second international break. Ahead of the trip, head coach Manuel Baum has called on his players to be disciplined, play with courage and believe in themselves. “We need to be brave both in defence and in attack,” said Baum ahead of the away fixture. The FCA head coach is well aware of Leipzig’s individual quality and strength as a team. He highlighted their strength in one-on-one situations, particularly out wide, as well as their ability to break quickly after winning possession. “They can go from defence to attack at incredible speed, and that’s not easy to deal with.” The key, he explained, will be to “nullify Leipzig’s strengths as much as possible without losing sight of what we’re good at ourselves.” Leipzig currently sit fourth in the Bundesliga table and were also in Champions League action during the week, suffering a narrow 3-2 defeat to Manchester City on Wednesday evening. However, Baum does not expect their busy schedule to make Augsburg’s task any easier. “Leipzig have a big squad with plenty of quality, and they can replace almost any player without weakening the team.” With that in mind, the FCA coach wants his side to be “solid and dependable at the back” while also “believing that we can win the game”. He also stressed the importance of consistency: “The important thing is that we keep working hard and keep performing at the same level. If we can do that consistently, the results will start coming again.” Three centre-backs unavailable Augsburg will be without striker Steve Mounié and three centre-backs for the trip to Leipzig. Juma Bah (suspension), Calvin Brackelmann (head injury) and Noahkai Banks (knee ligament injury) all remain unavailable. The rest of the squad is fit and available for selection. Dahmen named on Germany’s standby list Germany coach Jürgen Klopp announced his squad for the upcoming international break on Thursday, with Finn Dahmen placed on standby. The Germany U21 squad is not due to be announced until Friday. With Noahkai Banks still sidelined through injury, four other Augsburg players could be in contention for a call-up: Hennes Behrens, Arijon Ibrahimović, Mert Kömür and Anton Kade.
